samples.text:
The bar chart illustrate the proportion of male and female students who were studying in five different subject areas at one university in 2023.

In Engineering, male students was the clear majority with 78%, while female students were only 22%. Business also had more male than female, 55% compared to 45%. So these two subjects were more popular with men than with women.

On the other hand, women were the bigger group in other three subjects. In Education, 74% of the students were female and only 26% were male, and this is the biggest difference after Engineering. Also, in Arts the percentage of female was 62% and the percentage of male was 38%. Medicine was the most balanced subject, with 56% women and 44% men, so the numbers were quite close.

Overall, it is clear that men dominated in Engineering and Business, whereas women was more common in Education, Arts and Medicine. The biggest gap between the two sexes was in Engineering and the smallest gap was in Medicine.
samples.why: All key figures accurate · overview present but placed at the end · mechanical linking (Also, So, On the other hand) · repetitive vocabulary · several agreement and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The chart compares the proportions of male and female students across five subject areas at a university in 2023.

Overall, men outnumbered women in Engineering and Business, while the reverse was true in the remaining three subjects. The most striking gender imbalance was found in Engineering, whereas Medicine had the most even distribution.

Engineering was heavily dominated by male students, who made up 78% of the total, compared with just 22% for females. Business showed a similar pattern, although the gap was far narrower, with men accounting for 55% and women for 45%. These were therefore the only two subjects in which male students formed the majority.

In contrast, female students were in the majority in Education, Arts and Medicine. Education had the highest proportion of women at 74%, nearly three times the figure for men (26%). In Arts, women represented 62% of students, while the male share stood at 38%. Medicine was the most balanced of all the subjects, with female students making up 56% and males 44%, a difference of only 12 percentage point.
samples.why: Clear overview of main differences · key features well highlighted and logically grouped · good range of linking · some less common collocations · mostly error-free sentences with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The bar chart illustrates how male and female students were distributed across five fields of study at a particular university in 2023.

It is immediately apparent that the gender balance varied considerably by subject. Men formed the majority in only two areas, Engineering and Business, while women predominated in the other three. The disparity was most pronounced in Engineering and least marked in Medicine.

Engineering stood out as an overwhelmingly male field: 78% of its students were men, more than three and a half times the proportion of women (22%). Business also had a male majority, but a modest one, at 55% against 45%.

Female students, by contrast, clearly dominated Education, where they accounted for almost three-quarters of enrolments (74%), leaving men with just 26%. Arts followed a similar though less extreme pattern, with women comprising 62% of the cohort and men 38%. Medicine came closest to parity; female students held only a slight edge there, making up 56% of the total compared with 44% for their male counterparts. Engineering and Education therefore represented opposite extremes in terms of gender composition.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected · clear, well-placed overview · figures used selectively for comparison · cohesion managed smoothly · precise, flexible vocabulary · wide range of structures, virtually error-free.
